sampling_model.design: Four-block strong-factor panel experiment with one unobserved counterfactual mean and a donor-only spectral construction.
sampling_model.units: For each \(n\), the donor block is \(n\times n\), the target row is \(1\times n\), and the target column is \(n\times1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment masks the lower-right untreated potential-outcome entry; identification of its mean follows from the exact rank and span restrictions.
sampling_model.overlap: No target-loading lower bound is imposed; donor singular values satisfy \(cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known \(r\) and \(\sigma\); \(A\), its singular spaces, and both target loading coordinates are unknown and estimated only through the real Gaussian observations \(X,R,C\). The certified implementation first applies the measurable map \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) and retains an explicit encoding-exception flag.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives Gaussian entrywise inference under condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\).  The present upper guarantee removes that condition only on the canonical square one-target subclass proved by the embedding proposition; the local lower bound on this subclass transfers to any containing class because honesty on the larger class implies honesty on the subclass.
Theorems 4.1--4.2 give uniformly valid minimum-distance inference for first-order-degenerate smooth transformations from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator.
Appendix C proposes a first-order bilinear interval and states that analogous validity requires modified projected-loading conditions.
Residuals from computed SVD factors produce verified enclosures for singular values.
Truncated SVD has explicit first- and second-order perturbation expansions and normwise remainder bounds.

body.tldr: A strong donor block identifies the missing untreated panel mean as \(\theta_n=uA^+v\). The donor-only interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) retains the bilinear transition term through an exact conditional Gaussian reduction, covers uniformly without a target-loading lower bound, has expected length of order \(w_n=a_n+b_n\), and attains the Gaussian oracle constant along every first-order-dominant sequence. The corrected canonical comparison uses Yan--Wainwright's normalization \(\omega=\sigma(n+1)\), giving global noise ratio \(O(n^{-1/2})\) and local ratios \(O(n^{-3/2})\). A measurable dyadic encoding plus residual-certified directed arithmetic now yields the same coverage and length guarantees, including uniformly negligible numerical padding, under exact-dyadic public controls.

project_justification.gap: Existing four-block panel intervals are sharp only after a target-loading lower bound, while generic first-order-degeneracy inference assumes that the primitive Gaussian experiment and its covariance are already available. Neither literature controls donor-SVD target drift at the quadratic \(n^{-1}\) width or certifies floating-point endpoints.
project_justification.niche: Known-rank Gaussian strong-donor panels isolate a finite-dimensional bilinear reduced experiment while retaining the repeated-spectrum, joint-zero, and arbitrarily slow-transition cases that defeat a single delta-method normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the donor-conditional experiment, constructs an analytic outer interval with an observable donor allowance and bounded fallback, proves transition-order and every-sequence oracle length results, and supplies a certified implementation. The implementation measurably encodes the continuous Gaussian observations, constructs inverse candidates by residual-certified Newton--Schulz iteration, encloses invariant projectors with an explicit matrix-sign truncation tail, propagates noncommutative rounding error through a solved recurrence, and falls back to a bounded branch hull whenever the spectral decision is uncertain.

body.related_work: Yan and Wainwright (2024) supply the four-block spectral estimator, regular Gaussian interval, and lower-bound architecture. Under their variance convention the present embedded \((n+1)\)-by-\((n+1)\) model has \(\omega=\sigma(n+1)\), so their global noise quantity is \(O(n^{-1/2})\), while the local quantities in condition \(4.4\) are \(O(n^{-3/2})\); these corrected rates still verify conditions \(4.1\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\), and joint-zero loadings fail condition \(4.4\mathrm c\). The upper extension is only on this canonical square one-target subclass, never the full published class. Bei and Navjeevan (2026) supply the general first-order-degeneracy perspective, whereas the present contribution is the strong-donor panel transfer, observable donor allowance, all-sequence length theorem, and certified computation. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025) and CAST are the same-question consumers. Verified-SVD and floating-point references motivate individual numerical ingredients but do not themselves prove the combined coverage-preserving implementation; that claim is derived here under the stated exact-dyadic public-control model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The numerical theorem is for the abstract directed radix-two model with arbitrary signed exponents and exact-dyadic public controls. A non-dyadic refinable control requires a separate known uniform time-and-output-size modulus, inclusion of that modulus in the schedules and bit count, and propagation of the returned control interval. An IEEE implementation must still realize the stipulated exact power-of-two rescaling, exponent widening, outward special-function evaluation, and rejection of flushed values. The statistical model continues to require known fixed rank, known homoskedastic Gaussian variance, strong donor factors, and exact row and column span membership.
body.honest_scope: The result covers square strong-donor panels of known fixed rank with known homoskedastic Gaussian variance, exact row and column span membership, fixed incoherence, and bounded entries. It does not claim unknown-rank adaptation, weak-donor inference, approximate-factor robustness, dependence robustness, or inference for a realized untreated outcome. Its comparison with Yan--Wainwright is confined to the proved canonical square one-target subclass. Real Gaussian observations remain continuous and are passed through the measurable encoding map; only the public controls are restricted to exact dyadic inputs for the proved polynomial-time certificate. Arbitrary refinable public controls and a deployed IEEE implementation remain outside the theorem unless their additional moduli and exceptional-state checks are supplied.
